entry.label: Autonomy
entry.description: Autonomy is not independence. A viable part needs discretion, information and resources, while remaining connected to wider identity and constraints.
entry.canonical_definition: The operational freedom and regulatory capacity of a part to respond to its local environment without being reduced to a passive execution point of the whole.

profile.title: Autonomy
profile.canonical_definition: The operational freedom and regulatory capacity of a part to respond to its local environment without being reduced to a passive execution point of the whole.
profile.summary: Autonomy is not independence. A viable part needs discretion, information and resources, while remaining connected to wider identity and constraints. This entry concerns operational discretion within wider constraints. A claim about biological self-production neither assigns that discretion nor shows who may decide what.
profile.why_it_matters: Local variety usually outruns central knowledge. Suppressing autonomy can make the whole legible to the centre while making it less able to respond where the work happens.
practice_connections: give parts resources as well as responsibility
monitor outcomes without scripting every action
open_checks: Do not infer delegated authority from an account of self-production.
profile.editorial_note: Biological self-production and operational discretion are compared explicitly. This source-located distinction remains a candidate for editorial acceptance.
